title: REPDF: Repairing corrupted PDF files through font mapping and object relationship reconstruction
venue: Forensic Science International: Digital Investigation 56, 302061 (DFRWS EU 2026)
summary: State of the art that PDFPundit is built on: byte-level object carving + template PDFs with a full-font database; dictionary-scored font inference; 1,000-file synthetic corpus (C1-C10); 90.67% mean text recovery.

title: REPDF dataset repository (dfrc-korea/REPDF): 100 original and 1,000 corrupted PDFs
summary: Corpus README (commit e547d4d, 2025-12-18). Clone to /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf (1.6 GB, git proxy). Suffix per class: _header _xref _trailer _page_tree _object_header _font_mapping_loss _remove_fonts _remove_unicode_fonts _stream_zlib _partial_cut.

title: qpdf source code (qpdf/qpdf)
summary: qpdf (Apache-2.0) at 4eba958. Rebuilds a broken xref by a full token scan (last copy of an object wins; trailer = newest with /Root, else largest XRef stream); does not carve ObjStm; recovers /Length by endstream/endobj search or empties the stream; writes undecodable streams unchanged; ignores Adler-32; missing /ID -> empty; US-Letter MediaBox default. Test corpus: 717 qtest PDFs + 78 OSS-Fuzz reproducers.

title: MuPDF source code (ArtifexSoftware/mupdf)
summary: MuPDF (AGPL-3.0-or-later, COPYLEFT: behaviour only) at d587982. Full-file repair on xref failure or object-number mismatch; carves ObjStm headers; later copies win except ObjStm vs later uncompressed copy; stops scanning at the first unparsable object once a root is known; keeps partial Flate output, ignores Adler-32, 200x bomb guard; font substitution by name/flags. No public test corpus.

title: pdf.js source code (mozilla/pdf.js)
summary: pdf.js (Apache-2.0) at d52fdf4. Recovery mode indexes all objects by scanning; picks the FIRST valid trailer with /ID; ObjStm only via surviving XRef streams; tolerant endstream search (misspelled/truncated forms); treats empty font files as missing; glyph-name ToUnicode heuristics; comments link each workaround to a regression PDF. Test corpus: 982 PDFs + 459 externally hosted .link PDFs.

title: PDFium source code (pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium)
summary: PDFium (BSD-3-Clause) at 8ca5b73. RebuildCrossRef word scan incl. ObjStm members; highest generation wins, ties to later copy; /Length from nearer endstream/endobj, stream dropped if neither; Flate silently returns decoded prefix, 1 GiB cap; missing /ID -> empty; Arial-based substitute face. Test corpus: 341 PDFs + 562 .in templates.

title: Poppler source code (freedesktop poppler)
summary: Poppler (GPL-2.0-or-later, COPYLEFT: behaviour only) at c8dc23d. Line-start scan for trailer/endstream plus object headers, then XRef/ObjStm parsing; gen>= rule (ObjStm index used as gen); stream end from recorded endstream table after reconstruction; own inflater keeps partial output; base-14/system font substitution; numeric glyph-name heuristics; missing /ID -> empty. Test PDFs are in poppler/test (SRC-0506).

title: Ghostscript/GhostPDL source code (ArtifexSoftware/ghostpdl)
summary: Ghostscript/GhostPDL pdfi (AGPL-3.0-or-later, COPYLEFT: behaviour only) at a3cc9bd. One-shot repair that requires '%PDF' somewhere in the file; last copy wins, ObjStm members override, highest-numbered Catalog becomes Root; always verifies /Length and rescans; ignores Adler-32; enumerated error/warning taxonomy; missing /ID tolerated. No public regression corpus.

title: Poppler test-file repository (poppler/test)
summary: Poppler's test PDFs (83 files, mostly feature tests: signatures, forms, encryption) kept outside the main repo, commit 48b6219. Repository COPYING is GPL-2.0 for the harness code; per-file PDF licences unstated (NOASSERTION): analysis only, never redistribute.

summary: REPDF reference [1]. Not in Crossref (no DOI). Memory forensics of files handled by applications; cited by REPDF as carving motivation.

summary: REPDF reference [22] (co-author J. Park). Format-aware carving of multimedia files (AVI, WAV, MP3 and others); Crossref dates it 2011 (MTAP 61, 2012 issue).

title: Tool type identification for forensic digital document examination
summary: REPDF reference [23]. Identifies the tool type that produced a questioned digital document; producer attribution matters for producer-aware repair (GAP-002).

title: CPR: Corrupted PDF recovery algorithm for digital forensic investigations
summary: CPR (DFRWS EU 2026, same volume as REPDF, different group: Kim, Park, Park, Jeong). Cached from the shared local cache copy that scoping-fonts fetched from dfrws.org (same sha256); this agent's own fetches got 403. Only the object-carving passage was read here (CLM-0138). DUPLICATE: scoping-fonts cached and extracted it as SRC-0402 (verified claims CLM-0400..0414, CLM-0446); at merge, set this record duplicate_of SRC-0402. Lead from Parallel web_fetch excerpts (SRCH-0108): carves objects from raw bytes; adapts to producer 'generation methods'; FontDB plus Llama 3.1 8B validation; 655 synthetic samples; commercial-only baselines. REPDF does not cite it; 0 citations.

title: An Alternative Approach to Data Carving Portable Document Format (PDF) Files
venue: Journal of Cybersecurity Education, Research and Practice 2024
summary: Content-based PDF carving (title and journal metadata; not read). OA (CC BY) on KSU Digital Commons, but the PDF endpoint returned 403 to this container at fetch time and a Parallel fetch returned only raw PDF bytes. 0 OpenCitations citations. Must be read to settle still_open for GAP-054.

title: Improved recovery and reconstruction of DEFLATEd files
summary: Title-level: recovery and reconstruction of DEFLATE-compressed files; cited by Force Open (SRC-0127) as pattern-based repair of corrupted DEFLATE data that can partially reconstruct content using knowledge of the content (e.g. English text), and by SRC-0132 for mid-stream damage defeating reconstruction. Not read by this agent (sciencedirect 403); scoping-compression cached and read it as SRC-0301 from a dfrws.org copy, so at merge set this record duplicate_of SRC-0301. Earlier paper: Brown 2011 'Reconstructing corrupt DEFLATEd files' (10.1016/j.diin.2011.05.015, not screened). Direct prior art for GAP-005.

title: A forensic analysis of the Google Home: repairing compressed data without error correction
summary: Real forensic case: a Google Home NAND dump read without the SoC's undisclosed ECC. Corrupted gzip fragments are repaired by brute-forcing 1-2 bit flips with the zlib Adler-32 as oracle, lifting recovered data from 8.32% to 99.68%; ambiguous repairs are merged with three-valued logic (indeterminate bits). Read via arXiv 2210.00856 (author-modified version). Code: github.com/enssec/squashfs_bitflip_repair.

title: Force Open: Lightweight black box file repair
summary: Black-box file repair (DFRWS EU 2017): learns branches that behave identically for valid files and forces them when a viewer opens a corrupted file. Evaluated on PNG, JPG and PDF (viewer pdftotext, baseline pdftk) with synthetic random-byte overwrites; repaired sets overlap little with the baseline's. Read from the ETH Research Collection copy (CC BY-NC-ND).

title: Standardization of file recovery classification and authentication
summary: Title-level (not read, paywalled): a proposed standard classification for how recovered files were obtained, plus their authentication. From memory (unverified lead): distinguishes e.g. allocated, metadata-recovered and carved files. Closest forensic precedent to the charter's six provenance grades; 18 OpenCitations citing works, none on document repair (titles checked 2026-09-27).

title: Digital Investigation Techniques: A NIST Scientific Foundation Review
summary: NIST scientific-foundation review (2022) of digital investigation techniques: tool testing (CFTT), error rates vs systematic error, the error taxonomy (incompleteness; inaccuracy: existence, alteration, association, corruption; misinterpretation) and the risks of carved/recovered data (missing or mixed sources). Free US-government publication. DOI 10.6028/NIST.IR.8354 is kept as an alias because Crossref truncates its title to 'Digital investigation techniques :', which fails the validator's DOI-title match. Discovery: known from memory, then confirmed in the citation network (it cites Lyle 2010, SRC-0131; OpenCitations, SRCH-0105).

title: Sources of error in digital forensics
summary: Title-level (not read; OA CC BY but publisher and Cranfield repository both return 403 here): taxonomy of sources of error in digital forensics.

title: If error rate is such a simple concept, why don’t I have one for my forensic tool yet?
summary: Title-level (not read; OA at sciencedirect only, 403 here): NIST CFTT author on why forensic tools lack a single error rate. NIST IR 8354 (SRC-0129, CLM-0126) cites it for the systematic-vs-random error argument.

title: Syntactical method for reconstructing highly fragmented OOXML files
summary: Syntactical reassembly of highly fragmented OOXML (ZIP+DEFLATE+XML) documents: ZIP central-directory offsets place known clusters, DEFLATE continuation tests and CRC-32 pick the next cluster, XML structure filters false positives. 82.97% of Govdocs1/NapierOne DOCX files reconstructed from shuffled 4096-byte blocks. OA (CC BY-NC).

title: On the classification of questioned PDF documents — Attributing PDF documents to the tools that created them
summary: Title-level (not read, paywalled): attributes questioned PDFs to the tools that created them. Relevant to producer-aware repair (GAP-002) and to not destroying producer traces.

title: DEX: Digital evidence provenance supporting reproducibility and comparison
summary: Title-level (not read; sciencedirect only, 403 here): DEX, an XML record of digital-evidence provenance (which tools and versions produced a result) for reproducibility and comparison. Precedent for the per-repair provenance record (charter 3c); descendants include DFXML (10.1016/j.diin.2011.11.002) and CASE (10.1016/j.diin.2017.08.002), found among its 22 citing works.

title: Repair and Restoration of Corrupted LZSS Files
summary: Title-level (not read; gold OA at ieeexplore, not fetched): repair and restoration of corrupted LZSS files (LZ77 family). Barral et al. (SRC-0126) describe it as adding redundancy to LZSS without changing the decompressor.

title: Digital Evidence Certainty Descriptors (DECDs)
summary: Title-level (not read, paywalled): proposes standard descriptors for expressing the certainty of a digital-evidence finding; a candidate vocabulary for grading confidence in repaired content.

title: A contemporary investigation of NTFS file fragmentation
summary: Real-world measurement of file fragmentation on NTFS workstations; SRC-0132 cites it for DOCX fragmentation rates (CLM-0134). A named real-world damage source for DMG-006 (charter 3a). Not read; repository copies listed by Unpaywall (hdl.handle.net/2066/230703, research.ou.nl).

title: Recovering Text from Endangered Languages Corrupted PDF documents
venue: Proceedings of the Fifth Workshop on the Use of Computational Methods in the Study of Endangered Languages (ComputEL-5), ACL
summary: Human-in-the-loop recovery of the CID->Unicode map for endangered-language PDFs by aligning user-typed text with CID sequences; by a co-author of the DAS 2018 system.

title: Cryptogram Decoding for OCR Using Numerization Strings
venue: Ninth International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR 2007)
summary: Title: glyph shapes decoded as a cryptogram via 'numerization strings'. Detail (word-pattern matching against a lexicon) is from memory, unverified.

title: Learning on the Fly: Font-Free Approaches to Difficult OCR Problems
venue: 10th International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR 2009)
summary: Font-free OCR by document-specific cipher decoding; extended in the 2011 IJDAR journal version (SRC-0405).

title: Learning on the fly: a font-free approach toward multilingual OCR
venue: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition (IJDAR)
summary: Journal version of font-free, document-specific OCR via substitution-cipher decoding across languages.

title: OCR with no shape training
venue: Proceedings 15th International Conference on Pattern Recognition (ICPR 2000)
summary: Title-level: OCR by labelling glyph clusters from language statistics, with no shape training. Details unverified.

title: Solving substitution ciphers for OCR with a semi-supervised hidden Markov model
venue: 2015 13th International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR)
summary: HMM decipherment of glyph-cluster sequences with partial supervision; the semi-supervised setting matches PDFs where part of the ToUnicode map survives.

title: Learning to Read by Spelling
venue: Proceedings of the 11th Indian Conference on Computer Vision, Graphics and Image Processing (ICVGIP 2018)
summary: Learning to Read by Spelling: Towards Unsupervised Text Recognition (arXiv title). Unsupervised text recognition learned from unaligned text corpora (method detail from memory, unverified).

title: Limits on the Application of Frequency-Based Language Models to OCR
venue: 2011 International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR)
summary: Tesseract author on where language-model priors stop helping OCR; background for the fabrication risk of LM-scored decoding.

title: Improving state-of-the-art OCR through high-precision document-specific modeling
venue: 2010 IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
summary: Title-level: document-specific modelling to raise precision of OCR output. Method detail unverified (memory).

summary: Shows that glyph positions and advance widths left in PDFs leak redacted text; the same width/position evidence is a name-independent font and text fingerprint relevant to font identification (GAP-003).

title: Improved Text Extraction from PDF Documents for Large-Scale Natural Language Processing
venue: Computational Linguistics and Intelligent Text Processing (CICLing 2014), LNCS
summary: Text-extraction pipeline for building multilingual corpora from PDFs; possible source of real-world encoding failure statistics. Not read.

title: DeepFont
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia
summary: DeepFont: Identify Your Font from An Image (arXiv title; Crossref title is just DeepFont). Visual font recognition from text images (name-independent font identification baseline). Font-library size and scope unverified (memory).

title: HanFont: large-scale adaptive Hangul font recognizer using CNN and font clustering
venue: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition (IJDAR)
summary: Font recognition for a large Hangul font set using CNNs plus font clustering; relevant to scaling font identification beyond Latin (REPDF's corpus includes Korean).

title: KITAB-Bench: A Comprehensive Multi-Domain Benchmark for Arabic OCR and Document Understanding
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
summary: Arabic OCR and document-understanding benchmark covering OCR engines and VLMs, including PDF-to-markdown; a candidate external yardstick for Arabic recovery (GAP-004).

title: Devanagari OCR using a recognition driven segmentation framework and stochastic language models
venue: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition (IJDAR)

title: Hybrid word/Part-of-Arabic-Word Language Models for arabic text document recognition
venue: 2015 13th International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition (ICDAR)
summary: Sub-word (part-of-Arabic-word) language models for Arabic recognition: a direct alternative to whole-word dictionary scoring that fails on Arabic morphology in REPDF.

title: Nougat: Neural Optical Understanding for Academic Documents
summary: Transformer that converts academic PDF page images to markup without using the PDF text layer; open weights. Failure-mode details (e.g. repetition) from memory, unverified.

title: olmOCR: Unlocking Trillions of Tokens in PDFs with Vision Language Models
summary: Open VLM-based PDF-to-text system. From memory (unverified): it conditions the VLM on text/layout anchors taken from the PDF itself and ships open weights and a benchmark.

title: OmniDocBench: Benchmarking Diverse PDF Document Parsing with Comprehensive Annotations
summary: PDF parsing benchmark with comprehensive annotations. From memory (unverified): per-element metrics incl. text edit distance and reading order.

title: READoc: A Unified Benchmark for Realistic Document Structured Extraction
summary: Unified benchmark for realistic document structured extraction (PDF to structured text). Metric details unverified.

title: Do VLMs Read or Rewrite? On Transcription Faithfulness in Vision-Language Models
summary: Shows VLM OCR silently 'corrects' imperfect text (typos, artefacts) where traditional OCR transcribes literally, and releases FaithC4 to measure it: direct evidence that VLM text recovery fabricates content invisible to clean-text benchmarks.

title: Seeing is Believing? Mitigating OCR Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: KIE-HVQA benchmark of OCR hallucination on degraded documents, plus RL training that rewards refusing to read uncertain regions.

title: Confidence-Aware Document OCR Error Detection
summary: Analyses how OCR confidence scores correlate with errors across OCR systems and builds a confidence-aware error detector (ConfBERT); relevant to calibrated per-glyph provenance.

title: Deterministic Inference across Tensor Parallel Sizes That Eliminates Training-Inference Mismatch
summary: Engineering work on bit-exact LLM inference (batch/TP invariance in vLLM); context for charter §3(c)'s determinism requirement on learned components.

title: Flexible character accuracy measure for reading-order-independent evaluation
summary: Character accuracy measure designed to be independent of reading order; candidate order-robust component for GAP-008. Not read.

summary: Page-level assessment of text recognition end to end; from memory (unverified) it separates recognition from reading-order error.

summary: 2026 scientific-PDF extraction benchmark; checked only by title - relevant to whether GAP-008 is still open.

title: pdf-cmap-fixer: Repair broken ToUnicode CMaps in PDFs so extracted text matches the visual content (GitHub, piotrgulbis)
summary: MIT-licensed tool (created 2026-05-01 per GitHub metadata in the search result) that rebuilds ToUnicode from embedded glyph names and renders Private Use Area glyphs for manual labelling. Shows the practical cascade: glyph names first, human labels for PUA. Not verified in container.

title: pdf-glyph-mapping: scripts to map PDF glyphs to Unicode for complex-script (Indic) text (GitHub, shreevatsa)
summary: MIT-licensed Rust workspace (self-described as mostly abandoned) for fixing incomplete ToUnicode maps in Devanagari PDFs: dumps glyph bitmaps, shows glyphs in context for manual mapping, emits /ActualText; its README notes glyphs are in visual order while Unicode is in phonetic order. Not verified in container.
